# Judith Chapter 15 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_015_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When those who were in the tents heard it, they were amazed at what had occurred.

**2** Terror and trembling fell upon them, and no man stayed near his neighbor; they all scattered together and fled along every road through the plain and the hill country.

**3** Those who had encamped in the hill country around Bethulia also turned and fled. Then the sons of Israel — every warrior among them — poured out against them.

**4** Uzziah sent word to Betomasthaim and Bebai and Choba and Kola and to all the territories of Israel, and men who reported everything came; and all who heard rushed upon the enemy and struck them down.

**5** And Joakim the high priest and the council of elders of the sons of Israel who lived in Jerusalem came down to witness the good things the LORD had done for Israel, and to see Judith and to bring her greetings of peace.

**6** When they came before her, they all blessed her with one voice and said to her: "You are the exaltation of Jerusalem! You are the great glory of Israel! You are the great pride of our people!

**7** You have done all this by your own hand. You have done good things for Israel, and God is well pleased with it. Blessed be you before the Lord Almighty forever." And all the people said, "Amen."

**8** The whole people plundered the camp for thirty days. They gave to Judith the tent of Holofernes and all his silver vessels, his beds, his bowls, and all his furnishings. She took them, loaded them on her mule, and hitched up her wagons and stacked everything on them.

**9** All the women of Israel came running to see her. They blessed her and performed a sacred dance in her honor. She took branches in her hands and distributed them to the women who were with her.

**10** She and the women with her crowned themselves with olive wreaths. She went before all the people to lead the dance, and all the women of Israel followed her; and all the men of Israel followed in their armor, wearing garlands and singing praises.

**11** And Judith sang this hymn of praise before all Israel, and all the people with full voice joined in this praise.

---
*LOGOS notes: v. 4 — the list of towns (Betomasthaim, Bebai, Choba, Kola) are specific Israelite communities, indicating that the victory reverberates throughout the whole land. v. 5 — "council of elders" for gerousia, consistent with ch. 11 ruling. v. 9 — "sacred dance" rather than mere "dance" — Greek echoreusen in the context of a victory celebration has liturgical connotations; the parallel is Miriam at the sea (Exodus 15:20). v. 10 — the procession is theologically ordered: Judith leads, the women follow, then the armed men. The order inverts martial norms to show that this victory belongs to the humble.*
